content.title: How many episodes are left in ‘The Pitt’ season 2?
content.text: EntertainmentPublished: Mar. 27, 2026, 2:55 p.m.Noah Wyle as Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch and Isa Briones as Dr. Trinity Santos in "The Pitt."Warrick Page/MAXEach season of “The Pitt” takes place over the course of one 15-hour emergency room shift at the fictional Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center. So, how many hours are left in season 2 of the medical drama?There are three episodes left in season 2 of “The Pitt.” The season kicked off on Jan. 8 and will come to an end on Thursday, April 16. Luckily for the show’s loyal fan base, “The Pitt” has already been renewed for season 3, and it’s likely to return in January 2027.“I don’t know the exact [premiere] date but yes, the idea is to keep it on an annual basis,” Chairman and CEO of HBO and HBO Max content Casey Bloys told Deadline in January. “One of the big goals in putting a show like this on the air was to be able to bring it back annually, that is an important part of the equation.”Warning: Spoilers ahead for season 2 of “The Pitt.”The Pitt’s sophomore season has served up fresh crises, wince-inducing injuries and interpersonal conflict. The shift is Dr. Michael “Robby” Robinavitch’s (Noah Wyle) last day of work before a three-month sabbatical. It’s also his first time seeing Dr. Frank Langdon (Patrick Ball) since he was suspended for stealing benzodiazepines from the hospital. After completing a rehabilitation program, Langdon is ready to make amends. But Robby and Dr. Trinity Santos (Isa Briones), the one who reported Langdon’s theft, aren’t as eager to move forward. During episode 12, which premiered on Thursday, March 26, Nurse Dana Evans (Katherine LaNasa) confronted Robby about his unresolved issues with Langdon.READ MORE: ‘The Pitt’ star’s real-life wife set to appear on the showElsewhere in the episode, both Dana and Dr. Cassie McKay (​​Fiona Dourif) expressed concerns that Robby is courting death with the motorcycle trip he has planned for his sabbatical. Some fans think that Dr. Robby’s burnout and mental health struggles will lead to a motorcycle accident at the end of the season. One theory is that Dr. Robby will be a patient during season 3, while others think he won’t end up going on sabbatical at all.“I feel like the show has alluded several times to the possibility of Dr. Robby having a motorcycle crash, especially with how exhausted and emotional he’s been. His stress is clearly affecting his behavior too, being verbally abusive to his peers and students,” one person wrote via Reddit. “It all feels like deliberate foreshadowing.”Noah Wyle as Dr. Robby and Katherine LaNasa as Nurse Dana in "The Pitt."MAXAnother viewer argued: “I actually think they’ve been kind of beating us over the head with the motorcycle thing. Now that [Robby’s friend] Duke’s in the ER, intact, without a clear diagnosis, and calling Robby’s plan stupid, I don’t think there’s any chance of Robby leaving for his sabbatical at the end of his shift.”“The Pitt” cast also includes Supriya Ganesh (Dr. Samira Mohan), Taylor Dearden (Dr. Melissa King), Gerran Howell (Dennis Whitaker), Shabana Azeez (Victoria Javadi) and Sepideh Moafi (Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi).New episodes of “The Pitt” premiere on HBO Max on Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET.‘Chicago Med’ teases main character’s shocking death ‘The Pitt’ announces shocking cast changes for season 3Reality stars finalize dragged-out divorce: ‘Trying to make my life hell’‘Bob’s Burgers’ star seriously injured in fiery car crashSara Donnellan is the Trending TV News Writer for NJ.com.
